remoteScriptEcho.domain: HTTP(S) operands with js/mjs/cjs pathname or a verified WayX shared-script namespace, including MIME echo delimiters, query and fragment
remoteScriptEcho.outside: Local resources and remote JSON/data are not reclassified; extensionless resources need source-byte classification

lexicalBindings.domain: TypeScript-resolved local bindings, capture-free generated bindings, closed const request/response/script aliases, guarded same-context scalar && reads, immutable literal keys/string tables without decoder execution, including unrelated delayed readonly uses while the queried access remains top-level, Boolean-only logical guards, mapped context-presence guards, unused pure host-presence probes and pure source-host typeof/const branches with var-hoist preservation, localized source edits and nonescaping function proofs
lexicalBindings.outside: Escaping platform aliases, class-getter receiver identity, nonsequential const/TDZ uses, dynamic receivers, eval and Function construction remain blocked

completion.domain: Literal/conditional/spread result objects, closed object-returning functions with nonescaping call results and single-parameter $done forwarding wrappers with all callers audited, closed variables and static scalar body/bodyBytes/status/statusCode/url reads/assignments/deletion; proven QX string/undefined results require original response-body declarations; class-local strict receivers preserve native calls
completion.outside: Alias escapes, shorthand escapes, duplicate dynamic declarations, loop assignment, unknown/async returns, escaped function results, header/response mutations and dynamic property writes remain blocked

storage.domain: Explicit plain constant strings/concatenations/const aliases as keys; known nonempty JSON serialization writes and pristine Loon JSON.stringify results including undefined deletion; read absence may normalize under ||, ??, Boolean/loose-null tests or proven String/truthy branch guards, including fully audited local aliases
storage.outside: Strict null/undefined observations, stringification, implicit/dynamic keys, Loon empty-string writes and full cleanup remain blocked

headers.domain: Pure Object.keys(h).find with lowercase-literal equality or anchored literal case-insensitive exact/prefix regex, guarded readonly lookup and no key/header alias escape; lexical let aliases must remain readonly; target validates one string value per queried name/prefix
headers.outside: General object casing, duplicate values, mutation, output headers and framing remain unproven
headers.reason: Global lowercase proxies alter enumeration, overwrite case variants and can remove Host or mutate unrelated source behavior
headers.next: Extend exact per-field operations and real-client vectors without changing dictionary casing, duplicates or framing

qx.policy: Omit request parameters without a documented QX equivalent without throwing; record omissions outside author script files. This is an explicit semantic exception, not equivalent timeout/cancellation.

http.implemented: Callback-source bridge: seven methods; Surge/Loon keep strict explicit HTTP options and native timeout unit conversion; QX maps author-documented fields and omits undocumented optional request parameters. QX-source literal/closed-const String request fields and fetch calls support closed then/catch, success-field destructuring without rest/defaults, and locally caught await, numeric statusCode, ASCII or exact-offset bodyBytes. All retain explicit UA/Accept/identity encoding, <=64KiB and one active request; source Promise errors propagate and unknown QX fields are omitted on all hosts including QX itself
http.production: Shared callback-source and proven QX-source Promise programs publish only after every registered profile passes the authorized targets and native source host; ignored QX fields are recorded outside author scripts
http.fixtures: tests/support/http-contract-server.ts, tests/script-contracts.ts, tests/script-task.ts, tests/script-flow.ts, tests/script-flow-production.ts and manual tools/script-client-probe.js; no real-client result has been supplied

timeout.qx: omitted without parameter errors by user instruction; no request cancellation is claimed and no timer is invented

cookie.qx: auto-cookie default false on build 934+; older versions differ

tls.loon: insecure defaults true; ALPN defaults h1
tls.surge: explicit insecure option; never inherit Loon defaults silently

http.errors: QX rejected Promise reason.error versus callback error/response/data; missing response must not become successful null
http.next: Extend dynamic URLs/headers, escaped response objects, detailed error observations and independent real-client fixtures; undocumented QX request parameters remain omitted without error

webAssembly.reason: Identical JS glue does not establish WASM availability, module imports, memory or native ABI equivalence on all hosts
webAssembly.inspection: Literal WASM_BASE64/base64_wasm modules are decoded, hashed and compiled without instantiation, recording imports/exports per source; never execute author start functions
webAssembly.next: Verify exact module hashes and each target engine/module profile or replace the specific exported operation with independent pure-JS code and byte vectors; no empty exports

hostWebApi.reason: Surge standard WebAPI may require WebView; QX/Loon do not promise all same globals
hostWebApi.implemented: Scoped UTF-8 TextEncoder/Decoder and atob/btoa with direct use or closed one-hop const aliases and closed instances, pristine intrinsics, exact BufferSource views, streaming/fatal/BOM, encodeInto and standard Base64 validation; tested against independent native vectors
hostWebApi.outside: Legacy encodings, shared buffers, codec reflection/escapes, intrinsic mutation, compression, arbitrary Web APIs and full DOMException identity remain unproven
hostWebApi.next: Extend independently verified algorithms or establish each target engine contract; local author polyfills remain local code

notification.domain: Three text fields; explicit Loon openUrl/mediaUrl or String link maps to Surge url/media-url, and explicit Surge open-url/url/media-url maps to Loon. Only HTTP(S) media and zero delay are supported; target QX omits optional arguments without parameter errors
notification.outside: Source QX rich-notification options lack author-repository evidence in inspected files and remain blocked to other hosts; clipboard confirmation, delayed delivery, base64 media, sound and lifecycle are not equated
notification.evidence: Surge scripting/api.html notification options (iOS 5.11+/Mac 5.7+); Loon Script API notification section; QX sample.conf and sample-task.js document three text fields. No notification-delivery/device certification is claimed

arguments.domain: Declared Loon Boolean/number/safe finite-select objects bind to an existing typed Surge JSON payload; native Loon uses its actual object. QX omits $argument only with proven safe author fallback expressions. Literal String schemas require actual String input
arguments.outside: Unbounded macro String escaping, missing payload/schema, unknown properties, unsafe null/object aliases and dynamic argument consumers remain blocked

binaryInput.domain: Explicit stable binary profile and observed principal body reads map callback Uint8Array to QX ArrayBuffer bodyBytes with exact byte offsets; unflagged text retains body even if QX exposes bodyBytes too
binaryInput.outside: Unresolved dynamic binary mode, missing required bytes and arbitrary mixed text/byte observations remain blocked

capabilities.verification: Node VM, native ICU, file-integrity and classic-JS syntax checks are engineering evidence, not blanket iOS device certification
